## Frozen lifecycle contract

Retain signatures `seekFrames(frame: number | bigint): Promise<void>` and `play(): Promise<void>` and existing lifecycle tail. Track outstanding seeks synchronously at invocation, including seeks waiting behind other lifecycle work, and decrement in finally. Closed precedence remains first. While any seek is pending, play rejects a typed `EngineWebAdapterError` with new code `session.busy`, lifecycle phase and remedy to await seek then call play; it must not call AudioContext.resume at all. A permitted play retains its synchronous pre-await resume call for gesture permission. Do not move resume behind an async wait.

At the seek's serialized execution, distinguish actual running versus suspended context. Running seeks retain existing producer-ACK semantics and normal worklet application; do not suspend or prime/render them. For suspended seeks, await initial `feed.ready()` if needed (attachment is established by the control port while suspended), await the pump's seek ACK/full bigint generation, synchronously invoke the SDK `feed.prepareSeek()` without another producer seek publication in that handoff, then await genuine fresh prefill. No later lifecycle seek may interleave; ordinary same-generation pump writes may continue. SDK preparation proves consumer release/exact identity, not producer prefill. Initial seek-before-first-play must succeed while still suspended, without an audible quantum or context time advance.

Reuse existing bounded prefill deadline/abort pattern and existing per-source SDK `Msb1RingObserver` instances. Use bounded `pull` callbacks to verify full bigint generation equals pump ACK and first available chunk starts at that source's target (min(requested frame, declared frames)); do not accept WROTE, occupancy, low-word tag or initial attachment as generation proof. The suspended consumer cannot consume the observed live slot before play. Sources already at their declared end require no PCM; they must not cause an endless prefill wait. No copied offsets or consumer-index writes, new observation scratch, timers/framework or public pump operation. Keep actual EOF and active-seek behavior covered.

Bound all waits and retain close's immediate abort/reverse cleanup outside the tail. Preparation/refill failure must leave the session unplayable: close it through existing cleanup and reject the original error as the cause of a typed `session.seek` lifecycle refusal (add code/remedy), rather than clearing pending state and allowing resume. Close wins when already closing; no stale ready transition, swallowed numeric SDK refusal, unhandled late rejection or close deadlock. Validate ordinary invalid frame input without unnecessarily destroying a healthy session; only failures after entering paused mutation/preparation require terminal cleanup.

Document `await session.seekFrames(target); session.play()` and the gesture requirement. No mute/discard/silence quantum, target offset, counter reset, private package import, additional lifecycle queue or app raw ring access.
